newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean navy spots 14 Northern asylum seekers.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean navy spots 14 Northern asylum seekers.

text.p: South Korea said its navy on Monday intercepted a vessel carrying 14 North Korean asylum seekers -- one of the largest groups ever to flee the hunger-stricken communist nation.
A defence ministry spokesman said the boat was spotted off the west coast of the Korean peninsula near a military demarcation line that has split the two Koreas since their 1950-53 war.
It was not clear whether the boat had sailed straight from North Korea or had put to sea from China, an increasingly common jumping-off point for defectors.
It was one of the biggest defections ever from communist North Korea, where chronic food shortages are driving growing numbers of desperate citizens to flee.
The largest was a group of 17 -- including 16 members of a single family -- that arrived in South Korea last December after a six-week long epic escape down the length of China and into Hong Kong.
"The boat was spotted 5.7 miles (9.2 km) southwest of Paengnyong island," the spokesman said, referring to one of South Korea's northernmost islands.
Last Friday, a North Korean worker seeking asylum flew into Seoul from an unnamed third country.
